Flat search compares a query with all stored vectors: it provides exact nearest neighbors under the chosen metric but costs $O(Nd)$ per query. IVF partitions the space, probing selected clusters; fewer probes reduce work and may miss neighbors. PQ compresses vectors into subvector codebooks, reducing storage while introducing distance error. HNSW navigates a multilayer neighbor graph, trading graph memory and build cost for high-recall search. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.08281) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.09320)

$$M_{flat}\approx Ndb,\qquad M_{PQ,codes}\approx Nm\log_2(K)/8.$$

PQ's formula excludes codebooks and index metadata. IVF and PQ can be combined; HNSW may also index compressed representations. Benchmark recall against exact search, p95 latency, update/delete behavior, and RAM on representative queries. Recall is approximate-search recall, not proof that the embedding represents user relevance well.
